keys.label: Two alternating substitution alphabets for Feynman ciphers 2 and 3 (David Vierra)
keys.note: A1 = MANYREQUS.HVBCID.OLWGZX.K., A2 = JHAZTENYXMLOCUFBQVKPSGW.D.; used alternately word by word, even-length words reversed, word boundaries dropped. Published May 2023, re-applied here.

keys.label: Andreas Biragus (DECODE R5316, ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 no. 16)
keys.note: One sign per letter, signs for et and Francesco Piccinino; undescribed on DECODE (dated 1450 there). Connected to BnF ital. 1585 f. 33 on 29 Oct 2026.

keys.label: Filippo Maria Duca di Milano (ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 no. 23, DECODE R5323)
keys.note: Homophonic alphabet with up to six signs a letter, a full vowel-consonant syllable table, twelve word signs, about fourteen name signs and twelve nulls. Catalogued on DECODE with no names; identified for the Duke's 1446-47 slips in BnF ital. 1583-1584 (Oct 2026). A second copy of the same key is DECODE R1857 image 17.

keys.label: Filippo Maria Duca di Milano, second key (ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 no. 24, DECODE R5324)
keys.note: Homophonic alphabet with one to four signs a letter, word signs, code words for names and common words, six nulls. Catalogued on DECODE with no names; reads BnF ital. 1584 f. 15 (Oct 2026).

keys.label: Department of Texas route tables 1874 (rebuilt from the telegrams)
keys.note: Three word routes: no indicator (7 columns 1d 7u 4d 6u 2d 5u 3d), Baltic (9 columns 2,4,6,8,9,7,5,3,1 down), Dresden (7 columns 1d 7u 6u 2d 5u 4d 3d); arbitraries not recovered.

keys.label: Fifth Military District cipher example, Austin 1869
keys.note: Worked example of the route cipher with the indicator Pleasure, check words and arbitraries (Newberry, Grierson papers Ayer MS 3039 box 3 f. 153); gives the method, not the route tables.

keys.label: Marcolinus de Barbavara et Symon Arrigonus - Petrus de Pusterla (DECODE R1857 image 11, ASMi Potenze sovrane 1592 Cifrari)
keys.note: Homophonic alphabet, vowel-consonant syllable signs, word signs, nulls and a dozen code signs; several cells blotted. Identified for BnF ital. 1584 f. 69 by Satoshi Tomokiyo (2024).

keys.label: Port Sainte-Marie agent code 1729 (rebuilt from glossed siblings)
keys.note: One-part alphabetical French code, 379 values read off interlinear glosses in Huntington mssBLA 187-191.

keys.label: Soviet Moscow weather-cipher tables of 1940, as reconstructed by the Japanese Army Meteorological Department
keys.note: Four generations of Soviet weather-broadcast keys, 1938-1940; the Moscow tables of June 1940 are eleven rows of one 109-figure cycle, reported on 16 July 1940 and transcribed cell by cell by Brice Dudout (targets/moscowmeteo1940/key.tsv, tables_jun1940.tsv). Reports: JACAR C01004832600. Photographs not reproduced.

keys.label: Grand Chiffre of 1812 (the Great Paris Cipher), deciphering table SHD B n° 30
keys.note: Repertory of 1,200 numbers for letters, syllables and words, extended to 1,400 with additions for Spain (1211 the Army of the Centre, 1214 the English army, 1300 Lord Wellington, 1383 the Tagus), several numbers for frequent words. The French deciphering table is at the Service historique de la Défense (B n° 30); photographs published by Jean-François Bouchaudy (jfbouch.fr/crypto/napoleon). Cells used for these letters read by Brice Dudout, 226 of them first for King Joseph’s letter of December 1812 (bdudout.github.io/joseph-napoleon): targets/marmont1812/key_1812_entries.tsv. Photographs not reproduced.

keys.label: Philip IV's royal cipher of 1644-45 for Albornoz (key K1), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Syllabic cipher of the same kind with other values: letters for letters (a = c, c = n, f = r), numbered syllables in series of five (30-34 ma to mu), syllables written vowel first (ac = la, ap = sa). Rebuilt from AHNOB OSUNA,CT.2,D.16 (12 Dec 1644) against its plain copy of the time and tested on CT.2,D.20 (26 Jan 1645), transcribed before its plain copy was opened: 0.638 of letters against a p99 of 0.550; D.20 shifts the number series, so K1 is a family of keys (targets/albornoz1648/key_K1.tsv).

keys.label: Cipher of the Spanish embassy at Genoa, 1643 (key K4b), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Syllabic series of five numbers (27 fa, 32 ta, 37 as, 42 na ...), disguised bigrams and trigrams, single letters and a few code numbers (270 Vuestra Majestad, 223 republica). Learned by EM alignment on AGS Estado leg. 3598 nos. 38/37 and 41/40 (cipher and plain original), five values added from 15/14, frozen and tested on 3598,291 against 3598,290 (0.881 of characters, 0.834 of words). A different table from the 1638 Genoa key.

keys.label: Royal cipher A of Philip IV for the Marquis of Santa Cruz, 1629-32 (key K6A), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Homophonic syllabary with a nomenclator (numbers 1-99 for syllables and letters, 100-260 and letter groups for words and names), also used by the Infanta Isabella in Brussels. Learned by EM alignment on 14 cipher/decipherment pairs in AHNOB SANTA CRUZ C.50-51 plus the Infanta's letter of 14 Feb 1631 and its plain copy; frozen and tested on D.167 against its decipherment (0.752 of words, 0.857 of characters).

keys.label: Numerical syllabic cipher of Nuncio Biglia, 1565 (key K5d), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Digits written without spaces, words separated by 00: single digit = vowel or bare consonant, two digits = row consonant + column vowel, a few codes (59 qua, 97 che, 19 per) and a small nomenclator (11 S.M., 21 Imperatore). Rebuilt from the ciphertext alone by annealing, frozen and tested on a held-out part of letter 1 (lexical agreement 0.761 against at most 0.500 for 200 control keys).

keys.label: Cipher of the Albornoz embassy, 1648-49 (key K2), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Syllabic cipher: syllables written with the consonant changed and the vowel kept (mo = co, ne = de, ra = sa, la = pa), numbers in series of five (35-39 la to lu, 45-49 ra to ru, 50-54 ta to tu), single letters (2 = n, e = n, n = s, m = r) and code signs (cross = que, sal = Su Santidad). Rebuilt from OSUNA,CT.11,D.1 (Luis de Haro to the Count of Penaranda, 25 Sept 1649, enciphered for Cardinal Albornoz) against its plain copy of the time, lines 1-12, frozen and tested on lines 13-23 (0.859 of letters; permuted keys p99 0.476); 29 values added on the 1648 letter (targets/albornoz1648/key_K2.tsv, key_K2b_additions.tsv).

keys.label: Navy code of the Windward Islands, 1744 (key K5), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Two-part numerical nomenclator of about 500 values (syllables, letters, a few words such as 205 Dominique, 474 Royal), several numbers for common syllables. Aligned automatically from the interlinear glosses of six letters of Champigny of 1744 (ANOM C8 A 56 fols. 40, 44, 54-56v, 59, 63, 67), frozen, and tested on the held-out letter of 17 Nov 1744 (fol. 79): 0.894 of characters, 0.814 of words, against at most 0.578 and 0.122 for 200 shuffled keys (targets/champigny1744/key.tsv).

keys.label: Clave núm. 109, Secretaría de Guerra y Marina, issued to Gen. Rubio Navarrete (1913)
keys.note: Printed table of 160 numbers: letters (1-3 u, 13-15 o, 25-27 i, 37-39 e, 49-51 a, then 61 d to 93 z), syllables and military words (98 Gobernador, 106 tropa, 107 fuerza, 112 via, 132 General). The sheet is filed with the telegrams (CEHM DLXXIII.1.28.14-23); transcribed by Brice Dudout, nothing added (targets/rubio1913/key.tsv).

keys.label: Afonso VI-Vila Flor substitution of 1663 (K1-K3), recovered by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Letter substitution with homophones on Portuguese: numbers 2-53 and letter-like symbols (barred z = d, delta = i, long-stemmed B = n, barred 7 = h, overlined x = z; cursive x = c, h = l, n = f, r = g, a = p, d = x). K1 (30 symbols) recovered ciphertext-only from the letter of 26 May 1663 and frozen; K2 and K3 add ten homophones set on the 13 May letter. ANTT Luís de Miranda Pereira liv. 2 (targets/vilaflor1663/key_K1.tsv, key_K2.tsv, key_K3.tsv).

keys.label: Charles XII field chancery nomenclator K1710, rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Swedish one-part nomenclator of about 1,100 numbers in alphabetical order: letters 31-98 in two series, syllables 99-182, numbers 183-211, endings 212-304, words and names 310-1102; Denmark, England and Holland written in clear as B.B., LL, ddd. 334 values rebuilt by crib from a ciphered troop list and its clear draft in NLA Stade Rep. 5a Nr. 670 (fols. 73 and 82 against 74), frozen and tested on fols. 100 and 78v-79r (targets/stade1710/key.tsv).

keys.label: Anonymous Polish letter of 31 July 1662: substitution of 23 composite sign groups (key K443), recovered by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Simple substitution in which each letter is a group of three or four strokes; recovered by annealing on the front of the letter and frozen before the held-out reverse was decoded (targets/asang1662/key.tsv).

keys.label: Spanish chancery numerical syllabary of 1577 as used by Antonio Perez (key K_P2), rebuilt by Brice Dudout
keys.note: Number = consonant, mark after it = vowel, superscripts = final n, s, r, l; a variant of the table of the Genoa embassy, rebuilt on cipher and descifrada pairs of AGS Estado 1410 with five values learnt on Perez's own lines (targets/perez1578/key.tsv).

keys.label: Klucz Wąsowicza (i Kotowicza) do Alex. Lubomirskiego (DECODE R7501, ANK AKPot 3227 p. 81)
keys.note: A 1-100 grid on ruled paper with only the 25 values used filled in, one two-digit number per letter; a nineteenth-century reconstruction, not the key of the time, probably made at Krzeszowice (Łepkowski or Kluczycki). Checked on R7502, deciphered between the lines, and blind on R7508 by Brice Dudout (27 Oct 2026).

keys.label: Ferducci's 1532 nomenclator, from the glosses on his letters 2-2-9 and 2-2-24
keys.note: Three-figure numbers for names and words (543 Ferducci, 547 Martino Lucio, 518 S. Vito, 520 ambasciatore, 521 Francia), Q19 Ragusa, D-groups for months and the year; taken from the glosses written at the time over HHStA Türkei I 2-2-9 (2 June 1532) and 2-2-24 (18 Sept 1532) and frozen before use (targets/ferducci1532/decryption.txt).

keys.label: Key of Lope Hurtado's letter of 23 September 1520 (AGS PTR,LEG,2,36,2)
keys.note: The letter of 23 Sept 1520 is printed deciphered by Danvila (MHE XXXVI); a slip by the archivist J. Paz in the bundle names it as the key to the 10 December cipher letter.

keys.label: Lope Hurtado's Tordesillas cipher, 1520 (key K4, rebuilt from the letter)
keys.note: Homophonic letter substitution of about 37 signs (barred o = t, cross = s, 9 = a, long s = g, a T-shaped sign = z; some signs with two or three values), words kept apart, dotted sigla for persons; rebuilt from AGS PTR,LEG,2,36,8 alone, held-out lines frozen before use (targets/lopehurtado1520/key_K4.tsv).

keys.label: German embassy code (probably 0075), 82 groups from telegram No. 205
keys.note: Two-part four-figure code with prefix figures; 82 base groups fixed by aligning groups 0-146 of NARA 763.72111/4443 with the German text Bernstorff printed in 1920 (targets/bernstorff1917/codebook.tsv). Attribution to code 0075 probable, not proven.

keys.label: Hintze Ribeiro's code to Queen Amelie (1903), values rebuilt here
keys.note: Code of up to five figures (1347-67398 seen). 24 values from aligning the 11 May 1903 telegram (ANTT PT/TT/CAM/M15 m0003) with the decode written under it, segment by segment (27 Oct 2026, WAINUT); order alphabetical within page blocks of 100 with the lower pages reversed (hypothesis). targets/hintze1903/code_values.tsv.

keys.label: Venceslau de Lima's two-part code, 1909 (261 values rebuilt here)
keys.note: Five-figure two-part (randomised) Portuguese code, 06 full stop, 04 comma; 261 values from the receiver's pencil glosses on the eight telegrams of PT/TT/CAM/M09 (targets/lima1909/code_values.tsv).

keys.label: Sabugosa's alphabetical code, 1903-1910 (52 values rebuilt here)
keys.note: One-part Portuguese code: 11501-23400 = a-h, 0139-9019 = i-v; 52 values paired from the decodes of the time on m0009, m0008 and m0005 + m0004 of PT/TT/CAM/M14 (targets/sabugosa1910/code_values.tsv).

keys.label: MANCHESTERBLUFF, Confederate Vigenere key
keys.note: Vigenere on the tabula recta; one of the known Confederate keys with COMPLETEVICTORY and COMERETRIBUTION. On Johnston's telegram of 16 June 1863 it runs across the cipher words and advances by plaintext length (targets/johnston1863/key.md).

keys.label: COMPLETEVICTORY, Confederate Vigenere key
keys.note: Known Confederate key; tested on johnston1863 as a control.

keys.label: COMERETRIBUTION, Confederate Vigenere key
keys.note: Known Confederate key; tested on johnston1863 as a control.

keys.label: Greenhow symbol key, the copy found on her body (1864)
keys.note: Symbol alphabet with digraph, word and figure signs; found on Rose Greenhow when she drowned off Fort Fisher, 1864; copy 'Lamb Papers CXXIX' in NARA RG 45 M1091, naId 62017285 image 0484 (photostat 0485). Jordan wrote that he arranged the cipher in April 1861 (OR II 2 pp. 564-565). Table: targets/greenhow1861/key_1864.md.

image.caption: The key sheet found on Rose Greenhow, copy headed Lamb Papers CXXIX

keys.label: 'Confederate cipher 1864' symbol table (M1091 image 0483)
keys.note: White-on-black table in the same M1091 file (A = <, B = ^ ...); a different cipher from the Greenhow key.

keys.label: Puebla's First Cipher (Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Bergenroth's key no. 6)
keys.note: Letter substitution with second signs for a, i and u/v (a = q or M, r = the sign 46, t = R, s = barred T), reconstructed by Tomokiyo from Puebla's letters of 1496-1507 before he found the original (cryptiana, 'Spanish ciphers', Puebla1.jpg); Bergenroth's key no. 6. No sign for z.

keys.label: Puebla's Great Roman Numeral code (AGS Patronato Real leg. 52 doc. 33)
keys.note: An alphabetical one-part code of about 2,400 words and names numbered in Roman figures, on 200 PARES images (show/2207755); CC, CCC and CCCC written as ligatures told apart by a superscript o or an overbar. Tomokiyo published many of its values.

keys.label: Rakoczi envoys' reciprocal letter table (Harsanyi and Balogh), printed MHH XXIII p. 740
keys.note: Reciprocal substitution a=m b=i c=p d=u e=g f=v h=l k=x n=q o=y r=z s=t, f also for u/d; printed by Szilagyi at the end of Monumenta Hungariae Historica, Diplomataria XXIII (1874), p. 740, as the secret script used by Jakab Harsanyi Nagy and Mate Balogh at the Porte. Comenius used it in 1655.

image.caption: The table as printed in 1874

keys.label: Deboli's Polish syllabic code (St Petersburg, 1789-91), values rebuilt here
keys.note: One-part Polish syllabary of about 2,200 groups in alphabetical order, punctuation band 1775-1788. 630 groups anchored by aligning eleven 1789 cipher despatches (AGAD ZbPop 17) with their clear texts (ZbPop 419/417), 27-28 Oct 2026; probably the 'Cyfra polska' sent to Deboli in 1783 (ZbPop 444, not online).

keys.label: João IV–Nisa alphabet A, 1642-44, rebuilt here
keys.note: Latin-letter substitution with homophones for s and u/v, ⊕ = Castile, ft = King of France; rebuilt from the clear copies of letters 8, 9 and 13 in ANTT MSLIV 1017 (targets/joao1642/key.py).

keys.label: João IV–Nisa alphabet B, 1644-45, rebuilt here
keys.note: Greek-shaped signs, letter-for-letter substitution; rebuilt from the volume's list of deciphered passages (m0276) against Cartas 187 and 212 (targets/joao1642/key.py KEY_B).

keys.label: Martinique key for d'Ennery, 1765 (printed form)
keys.by: Secretariat of State for the Navy
keys.note: ANOM COL C8 A 67 f. 178: printed two-part nomenclator form, 800 entries, numbers filled in by hand, encipher and decipher tables.

keys.label: Windward Islands code of 1761 (La Touche and La Riviere), values rebuilt here
keys.note: Two-part numerical nomenclator, values 11-696. About 110 values from the interlinear decipherment of La Riviere's letter of 21 Aug 1761 (ANOM C8 A 63 f. 208), extended from context in the letter of 12 June 1761 (27 Oct 2026); key1761.tsv grades every value.

keys.label: Hesse-Darmstadt cipher alphabets of Georg II and Cardinal Friedrich (HStAD D 4 Nr. 141/2)
keys.note: Archive key file with alphabets of 1652 and 1658.

keys.label: Erbach's Lord's Prayer verse key (line, letter), rebuilt here
keys.note: Eight-line rhymed German Lord's Prayer, 'O Vatter aller frommen / geheiligt werd dein nahm / ...'; rebuilt from cribs in the contemporary Latin outline of the undated letter (27 Oct 2026). Line 8 known only as 'p?x'.

keys.label: Jefferson's Code No. 11 (Barclay-Lamb code, 1785-1791), values rebuilt here
keys.note: 348 values from Jefferson's interlinear decodings of Barclay's and Carmichael's letters, his clear-text sheets (1787, 1788, 1791) and the State Department decodings of Short's 1789 despatches (27 Oct 2026). The Jefferson Papers editors' partial reconstruction was never printed.

keys.label: Murray's legation code (The Hague, 1797-1801), values rebuilt here
keys.note: Values taken from the clerks' interlinear decodes of Murray's 1797-98 despatches (NARA M42 reel 4) and Wagner's decode of the 18 May 1801 postscript; six checked on the frames (26 Oct 2026).

keys.label: Mountflorence's one-part code (Paris, 1801), rebuilt here
keys.note: 25 values from the 18 March 1801 letter: 15 letters from the spelled names Luneville, Parma, Tuscany, Dupont, 10 words placed by the alphabetical order (26 Oct 2026).

keys.label: Alonso de Silva - Garcilaso de la Vega cipher (RAH 9/15 ff. 11-14v)
keys.note: Alphabet, name list and a large code of VC/CVC groups; on DECODE as key record R9822 (BRAH 9/15).

keys.label: Rome cipher, RAH 9/15 f. 16
keys.note: Latin-letter alphabet with superscript marks and a Roman name list (pope, College, cardinals); Galende assigns it to fray Juan de Mauleon. DECODE R9823/R9824.

keys.label: Schoning's symbol alphabet and code (1783-84), rebuilt here
keys.note: 24-sign alphabet from Van der Hoop's clear copies; one-part code, 188 of 226 numbers from glosses, his 14 Dec 1783 decipherment (A32-599) and De Larrey's Byland list (A32-604) (26 Oct 2026).

keys.label: Van Reede's code to Princess Wilhelmina (1789-92), rebuilt here
keys.note: Marked 1-3 digit nomenclator, 386 numbers voted from the interlinear decipherments of KHA A32-545-547 (25 Oct 2026); held-out 62% vs 10%.

keys.label: d'Yvoy - Hereditary Prince London code (1797-98), rebuilt here
keys.note: Dutch word code, 105 numbers voted from the interlinear decipherments of KHA A35-1450-1451 (26 Oct 2026); leave-one-page-out 78% vs 26%.

keys.label: d'Yvoy - Hereditary Prince code of 1799, rebuilt here
keys.note: Dutch word code, 50 numbers voted from the interlinear decipherments of KHA A35-1452-1453 (26 Oct 2026); leave-one-page-out 81% vs 27%.

keys.label: Philip II - Don Juan of Austria cipher (1574), rebuilt here
keys.note: Letters on 1-2 digit numbers near alphabetical order, vowel marks (cross e, dot i), codes pe/co/Lo; rebuilt from KHA G016-A0204 and its clear version (24 Oct 2026).

keys.label: Gara de Senisteros vowel cipher, rebuilt here
keys.note: Vowels as digits (4=a, 8=e, 3=i, 7=o, 2=u), consonants in clear; read off the first cipher line of NA 3.01.14 inv. 2442 (23 Oct 2026).

keys.label: St. Luc's Cipher (Tomokiyo's table, corrected by Brackx on BnF fr. 15572 f. 245)
keys.note: Tomokiyo's cryptiana table for Saint-Luc's ciphers of 1586; corrected and extended by Michael Brackx (issue #90) on the contemporary margin decipherments of f. 245r-v (Monsieur du Mayne, pour, la Rochelle, ss, la, rr, h, m). Several labels still carry two to four values.

keys.label: Rákóczi's Hungarian syllabic key (DECODE R446, Ráday Archives C64-4d2-25 no. 6)
keys.note: Hungarian syllabic nomenclator; DECODE's transcription corrected on the image (69 al, 71-74 an/ar/as/at, 35 ly, 296 Belgium). Found on 23 Oct 2026 by scanning the neighbouring key records R380-R520 against 18 glossed groups of R473 (16 agree).

keys.label: Keresdi Bethlen family letter cipher, rebuilt here
keys.note: Hungarian letter substitution with reciprocal pairs (c=p, p=c, g=u, q=t ...), recovered from the ciphertext alone by quadgram annealing on R4936 (23 Sept 2026); reads R4937, R4940, R4942 and R4938's spans. targets/transylvania1645/shared-key-hypothesis.json.

keys.label: R4939 paired alphabet (1648), rebuilt here
keys.note: A different simple substitution in another hand: 23 values, ten reciprocal pairs (a-m, b-i, c-p, d-u, e-g, f-v, h-l, o-y, r-z, s-t); broken ciphertext-only by annealing (23 Oct 2026). targets/transylvania1645/R4939_key.md.

keys.label: Henri IV-Brèves key of 1610 (BnF fr. 3462 view 112; DECODE R2077)
keys.note: Broken on R2077 by George Lasry with Biermann and Tomokiyo (2021); table found by Camille Desenclos in fr. 3462 (R2077 says 3642); Lasry's CTTS key adds a repeat sign (PR #61).

keys.label: R9424 letter substitution, recovered by Ryan Xu
keys.note: Simple substitution on Latin letters, / doubles the previous letter, nulls at word edges; recovered ciphertext-only from the repository transcription (issue #89, 23 Oct 2026); checked on the images here.

keys.label: Van Reede's 1792-93 marked code, rebuilt from inv. 6695 (WAINUT)
keys.note: Rebuilt from 44 cipher/clear pairs in NA 1.01.02 inv. 6695 (PR #66): 2,385 marked group forms; leave-one-out 0.599 of groups exact. A proposal.

keys.label: Viceroy of Sicily 1503, Espagnol 318 no. 94 (Brackx)
keys.note: Recovered from the ciphertext of no. 94 (GitHub issue #62): 39 homophonic sign classes for 21 letters; about 20 code groups firm from context (qa que, rah y, mny de, qag se ...), 14 tentative; two-part code. Close to the Gran cifra of 1501-04 (Bergenroth's muy = de).

keys.label: Louis XIII-Sabran cipher of 1631 (Lasry, BNF Francais 4134)
keys.note: Recovered ciphertext-only by Lasry with CTTS (2022) and published as an image on Tomokiyo's GL.htm ('Melchior de Sabran (1631)'); completed in 2026 (PR 84): 22 letters with up to four signs, 41 two-digit word codes, ten name signs, three doubling signs. Reads Baluze 155 f. 79 and the letter-books fr. 4134 and fr. 4135.

keys.label: Le Tellier-Marca cipher of 1644 (Tomokiyo's table)
keys.note: Rebuilt by Tomokiyo from the Le Tellier letters of 1644 in BnF Baluze 103 that carry decipherments of the time (ff. 171, 189, 200, 230); Cryptiana louisxiv0.htm.

keys.label: Vulcob and Ancel's Cipher 1575-1584 (Tomokiyo, frencheastern.htm)
keys.note: Homophonic symbol alphabet with double-letter signs, word signs and plain-letter code words; reconstructed from the margin decipherments of BnF Colbert 398. Additions by Harumi-Matsuba (uu, g, ff, nn, null c; saturnus = l'Empereur, Juno = le Roy d'Espagne).

keys.label: Tomokiyo's reconstructed table of Fiesque's cipher (French ciphers for German affairs)
keys.note: Cryptiana frencheastern.htm, reconstructed for BnF fr. 15919; values for signs outside the table inferred by Harumi-Matsuba (issue #52).

keys.label: Catholic League polyphonic cipher of 1592-93 (Tomokiyo, mayenne.htm)
keys.note: Eleven signs each for two letters (a/n, b/o ... m/z), signs for que, qui, pour, et and some persons; reconstructed from the League letters deciphered by the royal office.

keys.label: Guidi di Bagno, Paris 1652
keys.by: George Lasry with Astra and Opus 5.5
keys.note: Rebuilt from the ciphertext; CTTS ML transcription.

keys.label: Sforza letters 1446 (Maino reply, Amidani): Lasry CTTS key
keys.by: George Lasry with CTTS; refined by Astra and Fable 5.1
keys.note: Recovered from the ciphertext of BnF ital. 1583 ff. 68 and 70 (4 May 1446). Homophonic letters, up to six signs for I and O, word signs CHE, CON, ET, PER, QVA, SE; l, n, in provisional; 14 sign classes unresolved. Not the ASMi cart. 1597 no. 14 or no. 17 keys.

keys.by: George Lasry; GPT 6.1 Sol and Anthropic Opus 5.5 refinements
keys.note: CTTS ciphertext recovery; 49 observed entries, up to four homophones per vowel and three per consonant; one p/y class ambiguous. Related Kolosova prior work acknowledged, not applied as an alphabet key.

keys.label: Rusdorff 1625: homophonic table and alphabetical nomenclator
keys.by: George Lasry with CTTS and Claude Opus 5.5
keys.note: 24 letters, three two-digit homophones 24 apart (A = 16, 40, 64), letters 4 apart in runs of six; three-digit codes 187-760 in alphabetical order. Recovered from the ciphertext alone (PR 72); 2 codes unknown, 24 tentative.

keys.label: Saint-Luc 1586: homophonic table with syllable signs
